name: py-rle
instruction: Implement rle.py: def encode(s: str) -> str and def decode(s: str) -> str. encode run-length encodes every run as '<count>[<char>]', e.g. 'aaab' -> '3[a]1[b]'. Every run is encoded, including runs of length one, so the format is unambiguous for ANY input character including digits and brackets. decode is the exact inverse and must round-trip any string. decode raises ValueError on malformed input: a missing bracket, a count that is not a positive decimal integer, a count with a leading zero, an empty bracket, or trailing junk. encode('') == '' and decode('') == ''.
gateCmd:
python3 - <<'GATEPY'
from rle import encode, decode
assert encode('aaab') == '3[a]1[b]', encode('aaab')
assert decode('3[a]1[b]') == 'aaab'
print('gate ok')
GATEPY
verifyCmd:
python3 - <<'VERIFYPY'
from rle import encode, decode

assert encode('') == '', 'empty encode'
assert decode('') == '', 'empty decode'
assert encode('aaab') == '3[a]1[b]', encode('aaab')
assert encode('a') == '1[a]', encode('a')
assert encode('abc') == '1[a]1[b]1[c]', encode('abc')
assert encode('aa') == '2[a]', encode('aa')
assert decode('3[a]1[b]') == 'aaab'
assert decode('10[z]') == 'z' * 10

# Round-trip must survive digits, brackets and unicode.
for s in ['', 'a', 'aaa', 'abc', 'aaabbbccc', '1234', '3[a]', '[[]]', 'x' * 50,
          'mississippi', 'aAaA', '  ', '\n\n\t', 'ünïcödé', '中中文']:
    assert decode(encode(s)) == s, 'round-trip failed for %r -> %r' % (s, encode(s))

for bad in ['a', '[a]', '0[a]', '01[a]', '3a]', '3[a', '3[]', '3[ab]', '3[a]junk', '-1[a]', '3[a]]']:
    try:
        decode(bad)
        raise SystemExit('no ValueError for %r' % bad)
    except ValueError:
        pass
print('ok')
VERIFYPY
